summary: The change sets this repository up for Redline cleanly. The self-hosted guard case is small, well commented and covered by about 50 new rows, and the contract files follow the templates closely. Three of the four findings say the same thing: the self-hosted case promises more than the code delivers. A different case in the path gets past the new protection of the guard and hook on macOS. The syntax check reads only one of the four scripts. And a finding in the guard has no route that does not stop the run at Implement. The fourth is a nit: the unattended section is an older copy than its template. The repository has no scheduled or queued work (no routes/console.php), so no overlap applies.

findings.title: A finding whose fix is in the guard or hook has no route that keeps the run going
findings.description: In this repository the guard now refuses scripts/redline-guard.sh and hooks/hooks.json to every role (scripts/redline-guard.sh:199-201, CLAUDE.md:56). The unattended dispositions still give the shaper only fix, defer or ask, and every outcome except accept ends in an implementer task. A `fix` becomes a plan task, and an `ask` that the person decides as a change is applied by "a later agent" (line 35). The guard refuses the implementer's edit ("a person changes it, never a Redline role"), so the implementer reports the task under `blocked`. workflows/redline-loop.js:1351-1352 then throws a stage error. The round stops at Implement, and none of its other fixes is pushed or replied to. Nothing in this copy of the section, in agents/redline-shaper.md or in the workflow tells the shaper about this. The guard is the code in this repository most likely to draw findings, and R1-4 in this round is one of them. Question for the person: how should a run here handle a finding whose fix touches scripts/redline-guard.sh or hooks/hooks.json?
findings.proposedFix: Options for the person: (a) add a point to this copy of the unattended section, where point 11 was dropped, saying that a finding whose fix touches scripts/redline-guard.sh or hooks/hooks.json is always `ask`, with options a person carries out outside the run (fix by hand after the run and list it in the handoff, or accept); (b) change the workflow so that a task naming a person-only file goes to the handoff as a person's step and never reaches the implementer; (c) accept that such a round stops at Implement, and say so in README Known limits.

findings.title: The unattended section is older than the template it is said to come from
findings.description: The spec's shape.md Decision says this section "comes from the plugin's template ... with point 11 dropped and the gate numbers repointed". Diffing it against templates/shape-spec-unattended.md shows two more things missing: the "Every decision names its owner" paragraph after point 3, and the `decidedBy` and `recommendation` fields on each finding in point 10 (line 51), along with the sentence that explains them (line 64). The workflow's shaper schema requires both fields (workflows/redline-loop.js:276), and agents/redline-shaper.md:27 says the return shape "is given in the unattended-mode section". So a shaper in this repository is shown two different return shapes. The schema keeps the output correct, but the shaper's instructions contradict each other.
findings.proposedFix: Copy points 3 and 10 again from templates/shape-spec-unattended.md, keeping the repointed gate numbers and leaving point 11 out. Otherwise, record the two extra drops in the spec's shape.md Decision.

findings.title: bash -n scripts/*.sh checks only the first script
findings.description: Bash treats its first operand as the script to read and the rest as positional parameters. `bash -n scripts/*.sh` expands to `bash -n scripts/checks-template.sh scripts/redline-gh.sh scripts/redline-guard.sh scripts/redline-prefs.sh`, so only checks-template.sh is syntax-checked, and a syntax error in the other three passes the syntax check. The guard and prefs harnesses still run their scripts, but no check runs scripts/redline-gh.sh (none of tests/guard-test.sh, tests/loop-test.mjs or tests/prefs-test.sh names it). A broken redline-gh.sh therefore passes the whole gate. In a run on this repository the implementer may edit redline-gh.sh, and the github role runs it in the same round. Gate step 1 in shape-spec.md:234 says the same command "parses every script".
findings.proposedFix: `run_check syntax 0 "ls scripts/*.sh | xargs -n1 bash -n && jq -e . hooks/hooks.json >/dev/null"`. xargs exits 123 when any file fails to parse, and the command has no `$`, so the gate text can quote it. Use the same wording in shape-spec.md gate step 1. Reproduction: /tmp/redlinerepro/a.sh holding `true` and /tmp/redlinerepro/b.sh holding `if then`. `bash -n /tmp/redlinerepro/*.sh` exits 0, while `ls /tmp/redlinerepro/*.sh | xargs -n1 bash -n` exits 123.

findings.title: On macOS, changing the case of the path lets a role overwrite or delete the guard
findings.description: Before this change, the self-hosted case refused every path under the plugin's directory by prefix, so a case variant below the root (Scripts/...) was still refused. With line 221 skipping that check, only the case-sensitive tests at lines 238 (`fnmatch.fnmatchcase`) and 242 (`under`) protect the two files. `os.path.realpath`, which is pure Python on POSIX, resolves symlinks but keeps the spelling it was given. This checkout is on a case-insensitive volume, the macOS default: `ls .../SCRIPTS/Redline-Guard.sh` resolves. Tracing writable() for the implementer: `cp /tmp/g.sh Scripts/redline-guard.sh`, `sed -i '' 's/deny/allow/' scripts/Redline-Guard.sh` and `Edit HOOKS/hooks.json` match no protected pattern and fall under the REPO prefix, so they are allowed and overwrite the live guard or hook. `rm -rf Scripts` is allowed too, and it deletes the guard. From then on the hook command exits with a code other than 2, which Claude Code treats as a non-blocking hook error, so every later call runs unvetted. That contradicts README:135, "a run cannot loosen the guard that vets it". The same match predates this change for `.claude/redline*.json`, `.claude/settings*.json` and `.git/` in every repository (`.claude/Redline.json`). SELF_HOSTED (line 198) also compares paths case-sensitively.
findings.proposedFix: In protected(), compare case-folded strings: fnmatch on `path.casefold()` against `full.casefold()`, and fold both sides of the `under` checks for the plugin directories, PROTECTED_DIRS and PROTECTED_FILES. Folding always is the simplest choice and only refuses more on a case-sensitive volume. Add rows under `# @cwd PLUGIN`: `deny Bash cp /tmp/g.sh Scripts/redline-guard.sh`, `deny Bash sed -i '' 's/deny/allow/' scripts/Redline-Guard.sh`, `deny Edit HOOKS/hooks.json` and `deny Bash rm -rf Scripts`, next to the existing `allow Edit scripts/redline-gh.sh`. Add `deny Write .claude/Redline.json` to the ordinary section. All of these return allow today. In this repository the fix is to scripts/redline-guard.sh, which only a person may change (CLAUDE.md:56), so it cannot be a Redline plan task here (see R1-1).
